sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Candidate faithfully encodes the verified positive-shear applicability, owner paths, controlled direction, required operands, inclusive envelope bounds, MN-to-kN conversion, and expected-result-scaled formula tolerance. The repaired FILTER leaves the 0.6–0.9 LUI gap unaddressed while still checking FI = Cf × FIB for every positive-shear calculation case; deterministic validation is valid.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair the SPARQL envelope logic. The current FILTER treats every positive-shear calculation case outside the two stated intervals (including the 0.6–0.9 LUI gap) as a violation, thereby inventing an exclusive applicability envelope. Check FI = Cf × FIB for every required case, but constrain Cf to 0.0 only when position is within 0–0.6 LUI and to 1.0 only when position is within 0.9–1.0 LUI; do not reject an unaddressed position unless the verified requirement explicitly requires the case to lie in one of those intervals. Preserve the existing owner paths, controlled direction, units, and scaled tolerance.

Preserve the prior envelope repair, but also fix the formula SPARQL so an invalid longitudinal distribution factor cannot pass accidentally. Within 0–0.6 LUI require Cf exactly 0.0, and within 0.9–1.0 LUI require Cf exactly 1.0; if the applicable Cf is absent, wrong, or the derived FI differs from Cf × FIB (with the existing expected-result-scaled tolerance and MN-to-kN conversion), report a violation. Leave the 0.6–0.9 LUI gap unaddressed rather than treating it as applicable. The current second query filters out wrong Cf values before testing the formula, so Cf values such as 0.5 can pass.

Candidate faithfully encodes the verified positive-shear applicability, owner paths, controlled direction, required operands, inclusive envelope bounds, MN-to-kN conversion, and expected-result-scaled formula tolerance. The repaired FILTER leaves the 0.6–0.9 LUI gap unaddressed while still checking FI = Cf × FIB for every positive-shear calculation case; deterministic validation is valid.
